name: Open/Save MRU
purpose: Tracks individual files opened or saved through any application's standard Windows shell Open/Save dialog, spanning Office, browsers, chat clients, and most other common desktop software.
key_fields: "*" subkey - a combined MRU of the most recent files of any extension used in an Open/Save dialog
.<ext> subkeys - one per specific file extension (e.g. .docx, .pdf, .zip), each with its own MRUListEx-ordered entries
MRUListEx - binary DWORD-array recording access order, most recent first, at both the "*" and per-extension level
Value data - filename plus (Win7+) a binary PIDL encoding the folder path the file was opened or saved from
normal_baseline: Extension subkeys matching file types the user regularly works with, populated with filenames and folder paths consistent with normal document, media, and download workflows.
anomalies: A new extension subkey appearing for file types the user never normally handles (.ps1, .vbs, .hta, .scr, .iso, .lnk) around an incident window
A file opened or saved from a Downloads, Temp, or email-attachment staging folder shortly before other execution or persistence evidence appears
The "*" list and a specific extension subkey disagreeing on ordering or contents for the same time period, suggesting selective tampering
Entries for files that no longer exist anywhere on disk with no legitimate explanation for their absence
anti_forensic_notes: Because this key is populated by the shared Windows common-dialog control rather than by individual applications, clearing it removes evidence of file interaction across many programs at once rather than just one - a single deletion event with broad evidentiary impact. Entries survive deletion of the underlying file, making this a durable record of files that once existed even after they and any Recycle Bin trace are gone.
interpretation: The "*" key is a cross-extension MRU capturing only the single most recent files regardless of type, while the per-extension .??? subkeys retain a longer, type-specific history that can still hold an entry the "*" list has since rolled off. Reviewing both levels together, rather than just the "*" key, is necessary to recover the full file-interaction history for a specific extension of interest. Capacity: the "*" key holds the 20 most recently accessed files of any extension, and each per-extension subkey separately holds its own 20 most recent entries for that extension.
